The ATC is about **4.01**, from an outcome-regression estimate. The file has only observed outcomes, with no counterfactuals, so the answer depends on the estimator. I fit separate linear regressions on the treated and control arms, predicted both potential outcomes for everyone, and averaged the difference over the 608 control units.

Other estimators on the same data give somewhat different values:

| Method | ATC estimate |
|---|---|
| Outcome regression (T-learner, linear, all 25 covariates) | **4.01** |
| Doubly robust (AIPW, logistic propensity) | 4.07 |
| Inverse-probability weighting (logistic propensity) | 4.18 |

I did not run a formal standard error or bootstrap interval. The naive difference in means is 4.13, and the single-regression treatment coefficient is 3.96.

ANSWER: 4.01
